status: candidate; not accepted until an independent P1-INT-00 review passes

owned_paths: README.md - the foundation command section only; the rest of the file is not owned here
docs/program/tasks/P1-INT-00.md - status banner and handoff only
ownership.rule: Provider lanes consume these pins and commands unchanged. Adding or upgrading a root dependency, changing an image pin, editing the Makefile or creating a private command alias is a new single-owner task, not a lane decision (FF-01 sections 2.8, 3 and 6).

guards: the host interpreter must not be an active virtualenv (sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix is refused)
its reported version must equal .python-version exactly
UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never: no interpreter is fetched silently

uv.install: pip install --require-hashes from the pinned sha256 set below
uv.artifact_policy: Every published uv 0.12.11 wheel (18 platforms) is hash-pinned. The sdist hash is deliberately excluded: building uv from source needs a Rust toolchain that is not a documented host prerequisite, so a platform without a published wheel fails immediately instead of starting a surprise build.

runtime.note: --frozen never resolves and never rewrites uv.lock; a missing lock is a hard failure. The recipe contains no lock-writing command at all.

package_counts.method: lock_entries = count of [[package]] in uv.lock; third_party_locked excludes the auditmanager-foundation virtual root; installed_linux_x86_64 = .dist-info dirs in .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages. The 2 difference is colorama and tzdata, both gated marker = "sys_platform == 'win32'", so the same lock installs 22 on Windows.

runtime.cache_note: UV_CACHE_DIR and PIP_CACHE_DIR are pinned to git-ignored project-local paths (.local/uv-cache, .local/pip-cache). A bare `make bootstrap` writes no cache entry under the user's home - not ~/.cache/uv and not ~/.cache/pip - and needs no override. Measured: ~/.cache/uv byte-identical across a cold build and a second run (3407 files, 72984102 bytes, unchanged newest mtime); .local/uv-cache holds 3362 files after one cold bootstrap and 3363 at steady state after a second run.

governance.note: requirements/** predates P1-INT-00 and is NOT owned by it. It is consumed unchanged and is outside this task's allowed paths.

dependencies.note: Exact == pins only. Full transitive closure with hashes is uv.lock.

s3_client.note: Pinned so a bucket initializer that prefers the CLI does not have to invent a tag. The boto3 path in .venv is the alternative; P1-INF-01 chooses.

images.policy: Every image is pinned by tag AND multi-arch index digest. No floating tag and no 'latest' reference exists in the foundation. An image the lanes need that is absent here is a pin request back to P1-INT-00, never a local tag choice.

immutability.rule: The three image references cannot be redirected from any call site.
mechanisms: The effective reference is read at run time from this repository's Makefile bytes (`awk` over the `override FOUNDATION_*_IMAGE :=` lines), not from a make variable expansion. A make variable can be shadowed by a target-scoped assignment or re-overridden by a second -f makefile; the file's bytes cannot.
The Makefile still declares them with `override`, which defeats a plain command-line assignment and `make -e`.
Each value is rejected unless it contains `@sha256:`, so an un-digested reference cannot become effective.
.env is parsed as data, and naming any of the three there is refused with an explicit error before any service is touched.
immutability.changing_an_image: A pin request back to P1-INT-00. Never a lane-side or call-site choice.
attacks_verified_closed: make -e with the name exported in the ambient environment
MAKEFLAGS / GNUMAKEFLAGS carrying that --eval with a bare `make up` command line
a second -f makefile re-declaring it with override
.env assignment: plain, leading whitespace, leading tab, `export ` prefix, quoted, `+=`, `declare -gx`, nameref, line-continuation split, nested source

environment_contract.makefile_exported_note: Added by P1-INT-00 beyond the FF-01 name list so image identity has exactly one owner. They are injected into compose by the Makefile, are declared with `override`, and are REJECTED with an explicit failure if a lane sets them in .env.
enforced_before_any_service_command: a .env file must exist; no default is assumed
no reserved image variable may appear in .env; the Makefile's pins are re-asserted after sourcing
every frozen name must be set and non-empty
DATABASE_URL must agree with POSTGRES_USER/PASSWORD/PORT/DB and use the postgresql+psycopg driver
S3_ENDPOINT_URL port must equal S3_API_PORT, and S3_API_PORT must differ from S3_CONSOLE_PORT
MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD and S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY must be at least 8 characters

parsing.mechanism: parsed as NAME=VALUE lines; never sourced
parsing.rationale: Sourcing .env let it redefine shell functions used by the recipe, redirect PATH, or `exit 0` out of a target with status 0.
rejected: any line that is not a NAME=VALUE assignment or a # comment
an invalid shell identifier as the name

PATH, IFS, ENV, BASH_ENV, SHELL, SHELLOPTS, BASHOPTS, LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, PYTHONPATH, PYTHONHOME, PYTHONSTARTUP, PYTHONUNBUFFERED, UV_CACHE_DIR, PIP_CACHE_DIR, UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT, MAKEFLAGS, GNUMAKEFLAGS, MAKEFILES
parsing.value_semantics: no shell interpolation; one layer of matching single or double quotes is stripped; a trailing CR is removed

commands.forwarder_policy: A target whose implementation has not arrived fails with the reserved path, the owning task and the missing deliverable. There is no substitute implementation, no silent skip and no fallback.

pytest_invocations.effect: a literal `.venv/bin/pytest tests/integration/db` or `.../storage` imports foundation code from src/ with no PYTHONPATH override
pytest_invocations.rootdir: the directory containing pyproject.toml; pythonpath entries are relative to it
pytest_invocations.import_mode: addopts = ["--import-mode=importlib"]: test modules are imported by full path, so two lanes that both name a file test_checks.py do not collide with "import file mismatch" when their directories are collected in one run, and no lane needs __init__.py scaffolding.

import_contract.rationale: tool.uv.package=false keeps the repository from being built or installed as a distribution, so no build backend participates in bootstrap. These two root-owned mechanisms are the only supported import paths.
import_contract.forbidden: A lane must not add sys.path manipulation to a conftest or module; that works around this contract rather than extending it.
import_contract.consequence: A lane running a module by hand outside make must set PYTHONPATH=src itself; a literal pytest command needs nothing.

guards_proven_to_fail: missing uv.lock refused, with no lock regenerated and nothing installed

success_sentinel.rule: The owning task must print this line LAST - as the final actual output line, after its assertions pass. run_checked captures the checker's merged stdout+stderr with PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1, normalises ANSI colour, CR and surrounding whitespace, ignores trailing blank lines, and refuses both a zero exit status without the sentinel and any visible output after it.
success_sentinel.rationale: An exit code is not evidence. A stub checker exits 0, and a checker that keeps working after claiming success has a claim covering an unknown amount of later behaviour. Trailing blank lines are ignored; trailing output is not.
success_sentinel.also_enforced: A reserved path that exists but is zero bytes is refused as a placeholder.
success_sentinel.enforcement_limit: What is enforced is that nothing the checker WRITES follows its success claim. Work that produces no output after the sentinel - a detached child, or output redirected to /dev/null - cannot be detected by an output-based guard and is not claimed to be. PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 is what makes the ordering meaningful: without it the merged capture reflects stdout buffering, and a checker that logged to stderr after printing the sentinel would still look compliant.

known_limitations: No target other than bootstrap has been executed end-to-end: all seven forward to provider implementations that do not exist yet, so each was exercised only to its explicit refusal.

FF-01 mandates the literal paths .venv and .venv/bootstrap, so the governance environment is nested inside the uv-managed project environment. Anything that recreates .venv outside make (a bare `uv sync`, a manual rm -rf) destroys the validator interpreter; `make bootstrap` restores it, and the recipe order makes it self-healing.
load_env sources .env with the shell, so a value containing shell metacharacters must be quoted in the file. .env is operator-owned and git-ignored.

Locally the application authenticates with the MinIO root credentials. FF-01 section 4 excludes scoped service credentials and production IAM from this slice; the coherence probe therefore does not require S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID to equal MINIO_ROOT_USER, so a later scoped-credential design is not blocked.

pip index configuration is deliberately not neutralized, so an air-gapped mirror keeps working; only destination-redirecting variables (PIP_TARGET, PIP_PREFIX, PIP_USER, PIP_ROOT, PYTHONUSERBASE) are unset. --require-hashes still blocks substituted content.
3.12.3 is pinned exactly, so later 3.12.x patch releases, including security fixes, require a new single-owner pin task.

The sentinel guard is output-based: it proves nothing the checker WROTE follows its success claim, not that the checker stopped working. Silent post-sentinel work (a detached child, output sent to /dev/null) is undetectable this way.
`.env` values are literals: there is no shell interpolation, so a value cannot reference another variable. One layer of matching quotes is stripped.

UV_CACHE_DIR and PIP_CACHE_DIR are exported, not `override`-ed, so an operator may still point a cache elsewhere deliberately. The guarantee covers the bare command, which needs no override; an ambient value without `make -e` is ignored.

require_provider runs before load_env in all seven service targets, so while the provider implementations are absent the missing-.env and coherence guards are shadowed by the provider refusal and are not observable through a public target. They are live code: exercise them by extracting the shipped guards as described in verification.required_commands.

pyproject.toml is now a pytest configfile, which pins rootdir to the repository root and applies pythonpath and --import-mode=importlib to EVERY pytest run in this repository, including the historical tests/contract and tests/checkpoint suites. Those suites may not be run from this checkout, so the effect on them is unverified; the later task that makes them hermetic must re-check it.

fixed.B1: Image identity is read from the Makefile's own `override FOUNDATION_*_IMAGE :=` lines at run time, so it survives a target-scoped make assignment (--eval, including via MAKEFLAGS/GNUMAKEFLAGS with no visible command change) and a second -f makefile: a make variable can be shadowed per target, the file's bytes cannot. .env is parsed as data and refused outright if it names one of the three.
fixed.B2: Root-owned [tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath = ["src"], so a literal `.venv/bin/pytest tests/integration/db` imports foundation code with no PYTHONPATH override and no lane-local sys.path hack.
fixed.B3: run_checked compares the LAST actual output line with the sentinel, after normalising ANSI colour, CR and surrounding whitespace, and runs the checker with PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 so the captured order is write order rather than an artefact of stdout buffering.
fixed.B4: UV_CACHE_DIR is pinned to the git-ignored .local/uv-cache, and PIP_CACHE_DIR to .local/pip-cache, so a bare `make bootstrap` writes no cache under the user's home and needs no override.

also_fixed_in_passing.env_is_data: `.env` is parsed as NAME=VALUE lines instead of being sourced. Sourcing it let a lane's .env redefine compose(), redirect PATH, or `exit 0` out of a target and report success having done nothing. This channel was how the image pin could still be defeated, so closing it is part of B1 rather than new scope.
